utility.name: eBPF tracing tools
utility.author: Thomas Shaw
utility.description: Installs two eBPF tools that watch what programs do from inside the kernel. Aqua Security's Tracee (pinned release, checked against its SHA-256) records process, file and network events as JSON. Its built-in detection signatures (for example anti-debugging, fileless execution and rootkit behaviour) report suspicious activity as events. bpftrace runs short custom traces written on the command line. Both run as root, and Tracee needs a kernel with BTF (Debian 12 or later). With student_wrapper set to true, users without root can run sudo tracee-watch PROGRAM, which traces their own processes of that name (and any they start) with a fixed set of process, file, network and anti-debugging events, and nothing else.
utility.software_license: Apache v2 (Tracee user space and bpftrace), GPLv2 (Tracee eBPF programs)
